title: Choose Scaur's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Quad Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Quad Sheet
options.thesis: The store is printed like a topo map, and each layer of clothing is one colour plate of it.
options.viewport: The viewport is a quad sheet: a map collar with corner coordinates, quad name and scale bar framing an elevation profile from trailhead to ridge, the kit for each height pinned along it, and one red 'Build your kit' action.
options.risk: Contour lines are a common outdoor-brand backdrop; it only works if the map grammar does real work (legend, plates, elevation) rather than sitting behind the page as texture.

raised.raise: Layers switch on as registered print plates (base, mid, insulation, shell) you can toggle over the same map, not as tabs.
Size and colour pickers show every option at once; unavailable ones stay as quiet ghosts, and the chosen one is struck forward.
Conditions severity sets type scale: a 'wind 40 mph' rating is set larger than 'calm', so danger reads before it is read.
Stock and cart states print themselves in the legend's own type ('XL: 2 left', 'Added to kit'), never as floating toasts.
Photography is cropped hard onto the garment and the body wearing it, never the tiny-figure-on-a-ridge landscape.

options.label: Point Forecast
options.lineage: National Weather Service point forecasts and hourly weather graphs
options.thesis: The store reads like the mountain forecast you check before every trip, and your kit is the answer to it.
options.viewport: A seven-day forecast graph runs across the hero (temperature, wind, precipitation chance); pick a day and the kit for those conditions assembles beneath it with one 'Add kit to cart' action.
options.risk: Weather-dashboard styling is a familiar product-UI look; it can read as an app rather than an apparel brand, and it is the direction most runs here would reach for.

options.label: Stockroom Tags
options.lineage: industrial streetwear: quoted labels, zip-tie tags, hazard stripes
options.thesis: Every piece is labelled for exactly what it is: "SHELL", "MID", "BASE", in quotes, tag still on.
options.viewport: Giant quoted caps name the layer; a black shell on white with its orange zip-tie tag on; sold-out sizes take the hazard stripe.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and is apparel-native, and literal quoted layer names make the system very clear; loses on audience, because mountain buyers do not identify with stockroom streetwear.
options.risk: Reads as a streetwear pastiche if the quoting is decorative instead of naming the real layer.

options.label: Garden Vistas
options.thesis: Axial vistas and hidden garden rooms revealed in sequence.
options.viewport: A symmetrical garden plan with engraved capitals.
options.case: Fuses poorly: courtly formality has nothing to say to people buying rain shells.
options.kept: Registered plan overlays: layers now toggle as print plates over one map.

options.label: Cathode Stack
options.thesis: Every value present at once, the chosen one struck forward in glowing orange.
options.viewport: Ghost numerals behind a mesh, one lit.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a night-bench instrument is the wrong world for daylight mountain clothing.
options.risk: Dark, moody, and far from the trail.
options.kept: All options visible at once: sizes and colours show every choice, unavailable ones as ghosts.

options.label: Telop Captions
options.thesis: Outlined captions sized to the emotion of the moment.
options.viewport: Captions scattered over a frame at emotional scale.
options.case: Fuses poorly: comic energy undercuts trust in gear people rely on in bad weather.
options.risk: Noise where buyers need calm facts.
options.kept: Scale mapped to intensity: harsher conditions are set larger.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: One continuous transcript glowing on glass.
options.viewport: A typed dialogue as the whole store.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a terminal hides product photography, which apparel buying depends on.
options.kept: States print themselves: stock and cart status appear as text in place, not as toasts.

options.label: Scene Magazine Cover
options.thesis: A hard-cropped flash portrait under a hand-inked masthead.
options.viewport: Cover lines scattered at angles over a cropped face.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nightlife chaos fights both the audience and clear product choice.
options.kept: Hard crops: photos crop onto the garment on the body, not tiny figures on ridges.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The outdoor-brand store everyone knows: big mountain photography, white product grid, one bold accent.
canonCard.viewport: A full-width ridge photo with a headline and 'Shop now', then a four-up product grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the stores it would compete with, by design.
